record.original_question: A graph is called a cograph if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to a path with 4 vertices. A graph is said to be chordal if it has no induced cycles with n vertices for every n ⩾ 4. For a finite group G, the enhanced power graph E(G) is the graph with vertex set G and edges {x, y} for all x ̸= y ∈ G such that ⟨x, y⟩ is cyclic. (a) For a given integer n ⩾ 4, determine the set of all finite nonabelian simple groups G such that E(G) has no induced cycles with n vertices. (b) Determine the set of all finite nonabelian simple groups G such that E(G) is chordal. In(Preprint, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18073) we proved that if the enhanced power graph of a given finite group is a cograph, then it is also chordal. Also the finite nonabelian simple groups whose enhanced power graph is a cograph are described, and additional information is obtained on finite nonabelian simple groups whose enhanced power graph has no induced cycles with 4 vertices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph is called a cograph if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to the path on 4 vertices. A graph is called chordal if, for every integer n ≥ 4, it contains no induced cycle on n vertices. For a finite group G, the enhanced power graph E(G) is the simple graph whose vertex set is G and whose edges are the pairs {x, y} with x ≠ y such that the subgroup ⟨x, y⟩ is cyclic.

Solve the following two problems:

(a) For each integer n ≥ 4, determine the set of all finite nonabelian simple groups G such that E(G) contains no induced cycle on n vertices.

(b) Determine the set of all finite nonabelian simple groups G such that E(G) is chordal.
artifact.category_tag: Enhanced power graphs of finite groups
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a new entry in the 2026 Kourovka Notebook. Related work classifies finite simple groups with chordal power graph and characterizes finite nonabelian simple groups whose enhanced power graph is a cograph, with partial results on induced 4-cycles, but no complete classification of finite nonabelian simple groups whose enhanced power graph is chordal (or avoids induced n-cycles for general n) appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On groups with chordal power graph, including a classification in the case of finite simple groups
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies finite simple groups with chordal power graph (not enhanced power graph).
status_evidence.claim: A classification exists for the (ordinary) power graph case, but not for the enhanced power graph.

status_evidence.title: A survey on enhanced power graphs of finite groups
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing recent developments on enhanced power graphs, including cograph and chordal characterizations for nilpotent and some non-nilpotent groups.
status_evidence.claim: Open questions about chordality of enhanced power graphs of nonabelian simple groups remain in the recent survey.

status_evidence.title: Forbidden subgraphs in enhanced power graphs of finite groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies forbidden induced subgraphs in enhanced power graphs; partial results for simple groups.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial information on induced cycles in enhanced power graphs of simple groups is currently known.
